fields.text: Product photo to a hero ad, in three steps. 1) Edit drops your product into a scene and is told to keep the product identical. 2) Inpaint repaints only the brushed area (white in the mask), here to remove a second saucer that the placement step invented under the carafe, while the rest of the picture stays. 3) Seedance gives the retouched still one slow commercial orbit, and Video → frames keeps the last frame as a hero still. The packshot is generated so the example runs on its own; swap the first Image node for a 📷 Image input with your own product photo, then re-brush the mask on your scene. Inspired by @Genflickmovies' "one product photo into a hero ad in three nodes" (https://x.com/Genflickmovies/status/2112318819133702620).

Studio product packshot of a handmade ceramic pour-over coffee dripper: a cone-shaped dripper with a matte sage-green glaze, fine dark iron speckles, thin ribbed lines inside the rim, one small rounded thumb tab on the side, sitting on a matching round sage-green saucer. Centered on a plain white seamless background, soft even softbox light, a faint contact shadow, sharp focus, true-to-life color. No text, no logos, no labels, no people, no hands.

Place this exact coffee dripper into a lifestyle scene for a hero ad. Keep the product identical: the same cone shape, the same matte sage-green glaze and dark speckles, the same thumb tab and the same saucer, at the same proportions. Stand it slightly right of center on a pale travertine kitchen counter, with a clear glass carafe under it half full of coffee, a folded oatmeal linen towel and a small plain kraft paper bag of whole beans behind it on the left, soft warm morning window light from the left with long gentle shadows, a softly blurred cream-colored kitchen behind. Photographic, calm, premium. No text, no logos, no labels, no people, no hands.

fields.text: The clear glass carafe's rounded glass bottom resting directly on the pale travertine counter, with a soft natural contact shadow and warm morning light on the stone. No saucer, no plate, no coaster under the carafe.

Look: a calm premium product commercial, warm morning window light, shallow depth of field, photographic, the same travertine counter and cream kitchen throughout. Motion: one slow, smooth orbit. The camera glides in a gentle 30-degree arc around the ceramic coffee dripper from left to right at counter height, easing slightly closer, and settles on a centered hero frame of the dripper on the glass carafe. A single drop of coffee falls from the dripper into the carafe and a thin wisp of steam rises. Nothing else moves. The dripper keeps its exact cone shape, matte sage-green glaze, dark speckles and thumb tab. No people, no hands, no text.
